card.name: Qualifier words before symptom descriptions
card.fires_on: The words "new", "with" or "or" when they sit right before a symptom or clinical qualifier, as in "any new sign", "migraine with aura" or "asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic".

modes.label: "new" before symptoms
modes.description: The word new introduces newly appearing signs or symptoms to watch for.
modes.example: monitor patients on TYRUKO for any<< new>> sign or symptom suggestive of PML.

modes.label: "with" adding a feature
modes.description: The word with links a condition or measure to a qualifying feature such as aura or low blood pressure.
modes.example: migraine headaches<< with>> aura, or are over age 3

modes.label: "or" between severity terms
modes.description: The word or joins two descriptors of symptom status.
modes.example: in 806 patients with asymptomatic<< or>> mildly symptomatic castration-resistant prostate cancer

card.writes: It seems to push toward the word "feature" and its variants, which suggests a description of a characteristic comes next.
card.plain: It fires on small words like "new" or "with" that come just before a symptom or qualifying detail.
